bug_report:
Missed optimization: Lowering struct materialization into cold branches
Gcc optimizes sub-optimally for the following code:

```cpp
struct S {
    int& x;
    int& y;
    bool check() {
        return x < y;
    }
};

[[noreturn]] [[gnu::cold]] void bar(const S& s);

void foo(int a, int b) {
    S s{a, b};
    if(s.check()) [[unlikely]] { // very unlikely and cold
        bar(s);
    }
}
```

```asm
foo(int, int):
        sub     rsp, 40
        cmp     edi, esi
        mov     DWORD PTR [rsp+8], esi
        lea     rcx, [rsp+8]
        lea     rsi, [rsp+12]
        movq    xmm0, rsi
        movq    xmm1, rcx
        mov     DWORD PTR [rsp+12], edi
        punpcklqdq      xmm0, xmm1
        movaps  XMMWORD PTR [rsp+16], xmm0
        jl      .L3
        add     rsp, 40
        ret
foo(int, int) (.cold):
.L3:
        lea     rdi, [rsp+16]
        call    bar(S const&)
```

Struct `S` must be on the stack in order to call `bar()`, however, that's only needed in the unlikely case that the condition fails. Ideally the codegen should be the following:

```asm
foo(int, int):
        cmp     edi, esi
        jl      .L3
        ret
foo(int, int) (.cold):
.L3:
        sub     rsp, 24
        ... copy edi/esi to the stack and make struct S ...
        call    bar(S const&)
```

MSVC generates something along these lines, gcc and clang do not:https://godbolt.org/z/4axKfoe8xI can't simply write `if(a < b)` or delay the construction of `S` until inside the branch. My specific use case that results in code like this is [libassert](https://github.com/jeremy-rifkin/libassert), where an expression template is built from the user's condition and that is evaluated and inspected during assertion failure.

Even if the code is written as follows, gcc still generates sub-ideal code:

```cpp
void foo(int a, int b) {
    if(a < b) [[unlikely]] { // very unlikely and cold
        S s{a, b};
        bar(s);
    }
}
```

```asm
foo(int, int):
        sub     rsp, 40
        mov     DWORD PTR [rsp+12], edi
        mov     DWORD PTR [rsp+8], esi
        cmp     edi, esi
        jl      .L3
        add     rsp, 40
        ret
foo(int, int) (.cold):
.L3:
        lea     rax, [rsp+8]
        lea     rcx, [rsp+12]
        movq    xmm0, rcx
        movq    xmm1, rax
        lea     rdi, [rsp+16]
        punpcklqdq      xmm0, xmm1
        movaps  XMMWORD PTR [rsp+16], xmm0
        call    bar(S const&)
```

This may be a tricky optimization to perform, however, due to the above I expect it would benefit a large amount of code.
